entities.summary: Albrecht von Eyb was a key figure in the early German humanist movement of the 15th century, whose works helped shape the Renaissance in Western Europe. Born in the late 14th century, von Eyb studied at the University of Erfurt and became a prominent scholar, translating classical texts into German and promoting the study of ancient Greek and Roman literature. His translations of works by Cicero and Virgil were particularly influential, and he played a significant role in the spread of humanist ideas throughout Europe. The influence of von Eyb's work can be seen in the writings of later humanists, such as Erasmus and Luther, and his legacy continued to shape the intellectual landscape of Europe for centuries to come. Von Eyb's life and works serve as a testament to the enduring power of classical learning and the impact of individual scholars on the course of human history.
